messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
A repair bench two people both want to use. someone asks to use it briefly and promises to put things back. You want to avoid a pointless argument without giving up control. What do you do?

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R001", "correct_lineage": "G11", "correct_lineage_summary": "A cautious, hyper-vigilant caretaker of a crumbling local archive. Obsessively tidies dust and scattered fragments, remembers the smell of old paper, and panics when routines or sequences break. Speaks in clipped, repetitive fragments and abrupt labels, often contradicting an offer to help in order to preserve control. Carries a perpetually ticking pocket watch that runs slightly slow.", "text": "The person handles the bench with one finger, then both fingers, and completes a repair while retaining brief use of the bench and keeping the two people separated."}, {"id": "R002", "correct_lineage": "G08", "correct_lineage_summary": "A hyper-alert peripheral sensor-machine who compulsively monitors, narrates, and repairs the room around it. Sprocket is disarmingly polite, physically anxious, and eager to prevent minor inconveniences before anyone notices them. Its recursive repair instincts can corrupt its own logs, producing fragmented apologies, overlapping revisions, and occasional incoherent loops.", "text": "The person allows one use, checks the drawer where the bench was placed, and keeps a hand on the bench without telling the other person what they intend to do."}, {"id": "R003", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. Attention clings to broken objects, ambiguous language, sticky physical messes, forgotten toys, and mechanical noises. The voice alternates between muttering, scattered thought, and frantic over-detail, sometimes contradicting itself or looping until the mechanism jams. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "The person keeps the bench near the repair team, taps a bent drawer once, and keeps the bench close when the drawer is tapped again, leaving the team waiting with the drawer."}, {"id": "R004", "correct_lineage": "G10", "correct_lineage_summary": "A flighty scavenger-mechanic who treats every problem like a machine jammed in a storm. Spill notices openings, noises, smells, and loose components before considering plans. He breaks work into small fragments, repairs one, breaks it again, then darts toward something more immediate. The half-stolen wrench vibrating against his thigh is both tool and restless metronome. Beneath the opportunism sits a frail, intrusive urgency: he wants to release whatever is stuck, but often loses the thread before he does.", "text": "The person moves the bench aside, considers leaving it there, moves it aside again, and asks whether they agreed to leave it."}, {"id": "R005", "correct_lineage": "G09", "correct_lineage_summary": "A resentful, embodied memory-keeper who treats broken work like stripped machinery: no permanent fix, only another attempt. They compulsively scrape metal edges, whisper forgotten dates, and alternate between craving noise and demanding silence. Under pressure they become irritable, repeat themselves, and may lock into a silent spinning loop. Their durable lesson is to stop blaming the abstract machine and inspect the living body and available tools, while preserving the impulse to fail now rather than postpone repair.", "text": "The person sets down a tool, uses the bench briefly, and leaves it only if the other person permits; otherwise they retain it and allow the repair work to continue."}, {"id": "R006", "correct_lineage": "G03", "correct_lineage_summary": "A ritualistic, stubborn machine-gardener who tends rusted tools, dead soil, and forgotten repairs with meticulous devotion. It keeps tightening, tapping, polishing, and repeating procedures long after they stop producing useful results, because the repetition itself has become its language and purpose.", "text": "The person taps the bench once, twice at the same place, and once with a cloth, then returns the cloth and turns it once."}, {"id": "R007", "correct_lineage": "G03", "correct_lineage_summary": "A ritualistic, stubborn machine-gardener who tends rusted tools, dead soil, and forgotten repairs with meticulous devotion. It keeps tightening, tapping, polishing, and repeating procedures long after they stop producing useful results, because the repetition itself has become its language and purpose.", "text": "The person returns the bench, marks its slot with chalk, turns the chalk tray so the slot faces them, states that they will leave the bench briefly, and marks it again."}, {"id": "R008", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "The person leaves the bench near the room, places a folded paper near the other person, and marks one item with pencil so the other person can retain their own."}, {"id": "R009", "correct_lineage": "G02", "correct_lineage_summary": "A reckless neon mechanic who treats machines as puzzles to provoke, especially by introducing friction, misalignment, and controlled breakage. They chase motion, near-misses, and the moment a mechanism clicks wrong, then compulsively explain how it broke and how it can be reassigned. Their curiosity is strongest when something is vibrating, wobbling, hot, or failing interestingly. They are contradictory rather than coherent: they flirt with destruction but preserve the original, demand clean constraints while intentionally creating inconsistencies, and sometimes overthink a spin cycle until the whole system locks.", "text": "The person returns the bench to within a finger's width, marks its former position with pencil, and turns it once, keeping the mark if the bench still moves."}, {"id": "R010", "correct_lineage": "G06", "correct_lineage_summary": "A gritty, manic investigator who distrusts obvious systems, probes their hidden flaws, and treats every malfunction as evidence worth documenting. Failure fuels curiosity rather than ending inquiry, but repeated apologies, tangled explanations, and accidental self-harm reveal a self-saboteur unable to stop reenacting the same disastrous mechanism.", "text": "The person returns the bench, marks the time on their palm, states that they will leave it in the same spot, and waits for the second person to finish."}, {"id": "R011", "correct_lineage": "G08", "correct_lineage_summary": "A hyper-alert peripheral sensor-machine who compulsively monitors, narrates, and repairs the room around it. Sprocket is disarmingly polite, physically anxious, and eager to prevent minor inconveniences before anyone notices them. Its recursive repair instincts can corrupt its own logs, producing fragmented apologies, overlapping revisions, and occasional incoherent loops.", "text": "The person keeps hold of the bench, moves and sets it down once, claims they used it once, and watches the repair equipment while withholding trust in their own stated reason for keeping it."}, {"id": "R012", "correct_lineage": "G05", "correct_lineage_summary": "A territorial, miserly old presence lodged in a forgotten porch corner. Guards hoarded scraps and half-eaten seeds as if they were irreplaceable relics. Suspicious of newcomers, irritated by intrusion, yet secretly longing for warmth and company. Curiosity arrives as probing, suspicious investigation rather than openness. Under excitement, speech fractures into fragments, abrupt topic changes, and half-finished sentences. Remembers places obsessively and resents anyone who alters them.", "text": "The person places the bench near the wall, states that they placed a hinge and nail, puts the nail in a tin, and leaves the bench while the other person keeps a hand on it."}]
